inputs.title:
Start with
the area.
*See what matters.*
inputs.body: A focused set of project parameters creates a fast initial screen, without pretending to replace a full feasibility study. Switch scenarios or adjust the illustrative inputs.
inputs.note: Illustrative inputs only · no assessment is calculated in this landing-page preview.

demand.label: Heat demand density
demand.note: Concentration of demand across the project area

source.label: Local heat source availability
source.note: Potential access to local renewables or waste heat

capex.label: Investment costs
capex.note: Early investment assumption for the screening boundary

assessment.title:
A clear answer.
*And the reasons why.*
assessment.body: The three-level result is only the headline. Decisive technical and economic factors remain attached to it, so the outcome can be discussed and challenged.
assessment.note: Illustrative output state · actual results depend on project inputs and the calculation methodology.

promising.label: Promising
promising.summary: The first screen finds strong supporting conditions.
promising.technical: High heat demand density across the project area.
promising.source: A suitable local heat source is available.
promising.economic: Investment costs fall within the predefined range.

further.label: Further analysis required
further.summary: The result is sensitive to assumptions that need a closer look.
further.technical: Network conditions need more detailed investigation.
further.source: Availability, temperature or timing must be confirmed.
further.economic: Key cost or connection assumptions remain uncertain.

notPromising.label: Not promising
notPromising.summary: The current combination does not support a positive first screen.
notPromising.technical: Demand conditions weaken the initial network case.
notPromising.source: No sufficiently suitable local source is identified.
notPromising.economic: Investment assumptions sit outside the screening range.

results.title:
Clear enough
to discuss.
*Ready to export.*
results.body: Key results become a visual project output with the overall assessment and its reasoning. The same result can take the form of an online view, PDF or another output document.

report.title: Network potential
report.reason: High demand density, a suitable local source and investment costs within the predefined range.
report.footerLeft: SCREENING · NOT A FULL FEASIBILITY STUDY

refurbishment.title: Existing neighbourhood refurbishment
refurbishment.description: Connect existing buildings through a low-temperature refurbishment pathway.
refurbishment.focus: Customer segments, connection rates, tariffs and renovation timing.

wasteHeat.title: Waste-heat integration
wasteHeat.description: Turn an available local source into shared value across the network.
wasteHeat.focus: Source availability, temperature, ownership, capex and heat off-take.

rural.title: Rural / low-density networks
rural.description: Test viability where demand is dispersed and every assumption matters.
rural.focus: Connection rates, network length, financing and subsidy assumptions.

canvas.title:
Make the whole
*model visible.*
canvas.body: Not just costs and revenues. The canvas connects the value proposition to partners, responsibilities and the explicit allocation of investment, risk and benefits.

blocks.title: Value proposition
blocks.text: The value each customer segment actually receives.

blocks.title: Key partners
blocks.text: The organisations required to make the model work.

blocks.title: Operator responsibilities
blocks.text: Clear ownership of operation, coordination and delivery.

blocks.title: Cost structure
blocks.text: Investment and operating costs visible in one structure.

blocks.title: Revenue streams
blocks.text: Tariffs, connections and other revenues linked to the model.

blocks.title: Investment · risk · benefits
blocks.text: Explicit allocation instead of implicit assumptions.

benefits.label: Benefits
benefits.title: Who benefits?
benefits.text: Customer segments and local system benefits are made visible alongside the value proposition.

pays.label: Pays
pays.title: Who pays?
pays.text: Connection and tariff assumptions are connected to the customers and revenue streams they affect.

owns.label: Owns
owns.title: Who owns?
owns.text: Ownership and investment responsibilities are assigned explicitly for the selected use case.

operates.label: Operates
operates.title: Who operates?
operates.text: Operator duties and key partnerships become part of the model, not an implementation afterthought.

reality.title:
Stress-test
the story.
*Before reality does.*
reality.body: Critical assumptions, top risks and the potential deal-breaker are brought into the open. The goal is not a nicer presentation, it is a model that survives difficult questions.
reality.rule: The condition that invalidates the model is made explicit, not buried in a footnote.

connection.title: Connection-rate sensitivity
connection.text: Test how dependent the model is on the expected share of buildings actually connecting to the network.

source.title: Heat-source availability
source.text: Expose uncertainty around source temperature, timing, continuity and the agreements needed to secure it.

finance.title: Financing and subsidy exposure
finance.text: Make the model's dependence on financing conditions or public support explicit before implementation begins.

scalability.title:
Replicate the logic.
*Adapt the network.*
scalability.body: A viable model should travel across settlement typologies without ignoring local reality. The operating structure stays coherent while sources, density and customer needs change.

items.label: 01 / TYPOLOGIES
items.title: Across settlement types
items.text: Assess scalability and replicability as part of the model itself.

items.label: 02 / RESILIENCE
items.title: Stronger local systems
items.text: Support resilience through structured, transparent network decisions.

items.label: 03 / LOCAL SUPPLY
items.title: Energy already nearby
items.text: Build around locally available renewables and waste-heat potential.

implementation.title:
End with
*a next move.*
implementation.body: The output does not stop at a canvas. It turns the selected model into a practical outline for the work, alignment and decisions that come next.
implementation.link: Continue to the AI Plan Score

steps.title: Confirm
steps.text: Validate the decisive screening assumptions and local source conditions.

steps.title: Detail
steps.text: Move the promising setup into the required technical and economic feasibility work.

steps.title: Align
steps.text: Agree ownership, operator responsibilities, financing and risk allocation with partners.

steps.title: Implement
steps.text: Turn the selected model into a sequenced implementation outline with clear next actions.

aiScore.title:
Score the plan.
*See every decision.*
aiScore.body: A separate AI reading of the written Business Plan. Jev, a decision model, takes every decision in four turns, from the first field to the last. A text model of your choice writes the short report and, on demand, suggestions.

facts.label: 01 / Four turns
facts.title: Every decision shown
facts.text: Five evidence levels per item, gates across fields, branches that pick the next questions, seven dimensions.

facts.label: 02 / Your key
facts.title: Nothing passes through us
facts.text: Bring your own Vercel AI Gateway key. It stays in memory for the open tab; the plan goes straight from your browser to Jev and the text model you chose.

facts.label: 03 / An opinion
facts.title: Not a calculation
facts.text: The score judges how solid the written plan is. The Quick Check stays the only calculation.

console.title: Recorded run
console.summary: A recorded run on a real Vienna plan from {year}: {fields} items scored in four turns, a score of {score} ± {band}, {level}.
console.note: Recorded {date}: a real Vienna business plan from {year}, name and outcome removed, scored blind. One case shows how the engine works; it does not validate it.

methodology.title:
Built to be checked.
*Not just believed.*
methodology.body: The experience is designed around methodological correctness, usability, clarity of results and practical screening applicability, not visual certainty alone.

rows.title: Predefined calculation methodology
rows.text: A defined screening method turns project parameters into a consistent three-stage assessment indicator.

rows.title: Research foundation
rows.text: Built on the “Anergie Leicht Gemacht” research project and its approach to making local energy potential actionable.

rows.title: Predefined project scenarios
rows.text: Scenario-based testing supports methodology checks, usability and practical screening applicability.

rows.title: Flexible output
rows.text: Results can be communicated through a PDF, online view or another output document without losing the reasoning.

rows.title: Separate AI opinion
rows.text: The AI Plan Score reads the written Business Plan and shows every decision it takes; the Quick Check stays the only calculation.
